findings.issue: Missing resources are modelled as a { notFound: true } union returned from loaders and checked per-component, instead of TanStack Router's documented throw notFound() + notFoundComponent/defaultNotFoundComponent pipeline; this also forfeits the encouraged HTTP 404 and leaves no error boundary for non-404 API failures.
findings.suggestion: Throw notFound({ routeId: rootRouteId }) in the loaders (or beforeLoad), register defaultNotFoundComponent and defaultErrorComponent on createRouter, and delete the union types and the four per-route notFound branches.

findings.issue: 777-line module mixes the API client, response cache, domain types, shared card helpers and the data builders for all six pages; every route depends on it and it will only grow.
findings.suggestion: Split into api.ts (fetch + cache), types.ts (shared view types such as CardData/MoveRow), and one module per page's data builder; keep the queries.ts serverFn layer as the boundary.

findings.issue: Client components type-import shared view types from the .server module (also MoveTable.tsx:3, routes/pokemon.$name.tsx:5); it erases at build today but any future value import will break or leak server code.
findings.suggestion: Move CardData, MoveRow, MoveTableData and EvolutionNode into a plain lib/types.ts that both sides import.

findings.issue: No defaultErrorComponent is registered, so any non-404 loader error (API down, 500) renders the router's unstyled default error screen.
findings.suggestion: Register a defaultErrorComponent (and defaultPendingComponent if desired) on createRouter.

findings.issue: fetch has no timeout or AbortSignal, so a stalled API request hangs the server render indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Add AbortSignal.timeout(...) (or a small withTimeout helper) to apiGet and evict the cache entry on abort.

findings.issue: trackable, formatHeight, formatWeight and compareText are dead code, while the identical height/weight formatting is inlined at data.server.ts:588-589.
findings.suggestion: Delete the unused helpers or use them in getPokemonPageData; pick one.

findings.issue: Identity validators ((data) => data) give the server functions no runtime validation; they exist only to satisfy the type.
findings.suggestion: Either accept the input via a real validator (zod/valibot) or restructure so the loaders pass already-typed deps and drop the validator.

findings.issue: eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps with no comment explaining why the debounce effect depends on type/generation.
findings.suggestion: Note the reason (the effect must not re-fire navigation on unrelated filter changes) or restructure to depend only on query/search.q.

findings.issue: Move tables fan out one request per unique move (hundreds for a modern game) with no concurrency cap or batching.
findings.suggestion: Cap parallelism with a small pooled helper, or fetch lazily per column need; fine against the local snapshot API but fragile against a slow upstream.

findings.issue: The splat /$ route serves the not-found page at HTTP 200; the spec encourages a 404 status where the architecture allows it.
findings.suggestion: Once notFoundComponent is in place, respond with a 404 status (e.g. via the router's not-found handling on the server) instead of a splat route.

summary: A well-executed, current-API TanStack Start app: loaders, server functions, head handling and URL-driven filter state all follow the framework's documented patterns, and I found no correctness bugs. The one systematic deviation is a hand-rolled notFound union across all detail routes where the framework provides notFound()/notFoundComponent, plus a 777-line god data module. I'd request one round of changes — adopt the framework's 404 pipeline and split the data layer — then merge.
